content:
The [HSA Calculator](/hsa-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Project your Health Savings Account balance and check the 2025 contribution limits. Enter your coverage, your age, current HSA balance, annual contribution, years until you use it and annual return and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Project how a Health Savings Account (HSA) grows: tax-deductible contributions, tax-free growth and tax-free withdrawals for medical expenses — the only triple-tax-advantaged account in the US tax code. For 2025 the contribution limits are $4,300 for self-only coverage and $8,550 for family coverage, plus a $1,000 catch-up if you are 55 or older. You need a high-deductible health plan to contribute. This is a projection, not financial advice: real returns vary, and the limits change most years.

## How to use the HSA Calculator

Start by choosing your coverage from the list, then entering your your age, entering your current HSA balance ($), entering your annual contribution ($), entering your years until you use it and finally entering your annual return (%). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Choose your coverage (self-only or family) and your age.
2. Enter your current balance, yearly contribution, time horizon and expected return.
3. Read the projected balance — and check your contribution against the 2025 limit.

## Formula

Future value = balance × (1 + r)ⁿ + contribution × ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1) ÷ r, where r is the annual return and n is the number of years. The 2025 limits are $4,300 (self-only) or $8,550 (family), plus $1,000 catch-up at 55+.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [HSA Calculator](/hsa-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A family plan with a $5,000 balance, $8,000 contributed each year and a 7% return for 20 years grows to about $347,313 — $160,000 of contributions and about $182,313 of growth. The $8,000 contribution is inside the $8,550 family limit for 2025. Try the same figures in the [HSA Calculator](/hsa-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Coverage: Family, Your age: 40, Current HSA balance: 5000 $, Annual contribution: 8000 $, Years until you use it: 20, Annual return: 7 %), the [HSA Calculator](/hsa-calculator) returns Projected HSA balance: $347,312.36, Your contributions: $160,000, Investment growth: $182,312.36, 2025 contribution limit: $8,550 — your contribution fits. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Why an HSA is triple tax-advantaged

Contributions are tax-deductible, the money grows tax-free, and withdrawals for qualified medical expenses are tax-free too. No other account does all three: a 401(k) taxes withdrawals, a Roth taxes contributions. After 65 you can also withdraw for anything (paying ordinary income tax, like a 401(k)), which is why many people treat an HSA as a stealth retirement account and pay small medical bills out of pocket to let it grow.

## The catch-up and the limits

The 2025 limits are $4,300 for self-only coverage and $8,550 for family coverage. From age 55 you may add $1,000 a year on top. Contributions above the limit are taxed and penalised, so the calculator flags them. You can only contribute while you are covered by a qualifying high-deductible health plan, and your employer's contributions count toward the same limit.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Contribute the maximum if you can — the tax break is the best available.
- Pay small medical bills out of pocket and let the HSA compound.
- Keep receipts: you can reimburse yourself for old expenses years later.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the HSA contribution limit for 2025?

$4,300 for self-only coverage and $8,550 for family coverage, plus $1,000 a year from age 55. Employer contributions count toward the same limit. Try it with your own numbers in the [HSA Calculator](/hsa-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Do I need a special health plan for an HSA?

Yes — you must be covered by a qualifying high-deductible health plan (HDHP). A regular low-deductible plan does not qualify. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.

### What happens to my HSA if I change jobs?

Nothing — the account is yours, not your employer's. It stays with you, and the balance rolls over every year; there is no use-it-or-lose-it rule. Try it with your own numbers in the [HSA Calculator](/hsa-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can I use HSA money for non-medical expenses?

Before 65, non-medical withdrawals are taxed plus a 20% penalty. From 65 they are taxed as ordinary income (like a 401(k)) with no penalty. Try it with your own numbers in the [HSA Calculator](/hsa-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
